fact: Barn owls can hunt in darkness by using extremely sensitive hearing.
Great horned owls have feather tufts that look like ears but are not their actual ears.
Eastern screech-owls can hide well against tree bark because of their mottled feathers.
Burrowing owls often live in underground burrows and may be active around dusk.
Tawny owls are woodland hunters with excellent night vision and hearing.
Snowy owls may hunt during daylight in Arctic summers where the sun stays up for long periods.
Long-eared owls have tall feather tufts and often rest quietly in dense trees during the day.
Short-eared owls often hunt low over open fields at dawn and dusk.
Little owls are small owls that may perch on posts while watching for prey.
Nightjars have wide mouths that help them catch flying insects.
Nighthawks catch insects while flying and are most active around evening.
Kakapos are flightless parrots from New Zealand that are active mostly at night.
Kiwis use long beaks and sensitive nostrils to search for food on the forest floor.
Tarsiers have enormous eyes that help them see in low light.
Aye-ayes use a long middle finger to find insects hidden inside wood.
Slow lorises are small primates with large eyes adapted for nighttime activity.
Bushbabies can make powerful leaps between branches at night.
Mouse lemurs are tiny nocturnal primates from Madagascar.
Raccoons use sensitive front paws to explore food and objects.
Opossums are the only marsupials native to the United States and Canada.
Skunks can spray a strong-smelling liquid when they feel threatened.
Badgers are strong diggers that often rest in underground burrows.
Hedgehogs can curl into a tight ball to protect themselves with their spines.
Porcupines are covered with modified hairs called quills.
Many armadillos search for insects at night using a strong sense of smell.
Fennec foxes have huge ears that help them hear prey and release body heat.
Red foxes use their large ears to locate small animals hidden in grass or snow.
Gray foxes are unusual canids because they can climb trees.
Coyotes communicate with yips, barks, and howls.
Bobcats are stealthy cats that often hunt around dawn, dusk, and nighttime.
Leopards are powerful climbers and often rest or store food in trees.
Clouded leopards have long tails that help them balance while climbing.
Black-footed cats are small African wild cats that hunt mostly at night.
Pallas's cats have thick fur and rounded ears that help them blend into rocky habitats.
Binturongs use long prehensile tails to help grip branches.

Genets are agile nighttime hunters with long spotted bodies and ringed tails.
Kinkajous use long tongues to reach fruit and nectar.
Sugar gliders can glide between trees using skin stretched between their legs.

Vampire bats can detect warm spots on the skin of their prey.
Many fruit bats use their keen senses to find ripe fruit at night.
Little brown bats use echolocation to catch insects in darkness.

Fireflies make light with a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.
Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light because of chemicals in their outer covering.

Katydids often call after dark by rubbing parts of their wings together.
Male crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together.

Leopard geckos have movable eyelids and store fat in their tails.
Ball pythons are most active at night and may curl into a ball when frightened.
Boa constrictors use heat-sensitive pits to help detect warm animals.
Axolotls are aquatic salamanders that keep their feathery external gills as adults.
